analysis:
MARKET REGIME: SPY in uptrend with positive 20d slope — constructive backdrop, but not a license to force trades given the portfolio's deeply negative track record (9.1% win rate, 0.03 profit factor, Sortino -14.86). The primary job here is capital preservation and discipline, not manufacturing activity.

EXISTING POSITION REVIEW:
- NVDA: Only winner (+5.71%). On screened candidate list, uptrend intact, thesis holds. Hold and trail stop.
- AMP: -9.31%, stopped out twice in prior cycles, NOT on today's screened candidate list (implies trend deterioration or quality flag). This is a thesis-break signal. The position is small ($9,427) but the pattern of repeated losses on this name is a red flag. Strongly consider exiting on any bounce to limit further erosion. No formal SELL trade proposed here as it falls outside the candidate universe, but this should be reviewed manually for an exit.
- BR: -3.36%, not on screened list. Not in crisis but deserves monitoring; if it slips further below stop territory, exit cleanly.
- FOXA: -0.93%, essentially flat. Not on screened list. Hold but watch.
- MCO: -2.69%, not on screened list. Mild drawdown, thesis unclear from screening data.

NEW TRADE: One high-conviction setup identified. IT (Gartner) ranks #1 on setup score — basing at 44% of 52-week range in confirmed uptrend, extremely attractive forward valuation (fwd P/E 11.35, PEG 0.75), strong ROE and FCF, positive EPS revisions (+6.9%). This is the clearest Stage 1-to-Stage 2 transition candidate on the list. The one trade fits within remaining headroom ($28,818) and keeps total positions at 6 which is slightly above preferred 3-5 — justified only because NVDA is a clear hold and one trade is being added with proper sizing. If AMP is exited, this returns to 5 positions.

All energy names (MPC, PSX, CVX, APA) are 80-87%+ of 52w range — late-cycle extended entries, avoided per rules. KEYS and ZBRA at 94% range also avoided. ADBE and BX below SMA50 materially — not confirmed uptrends. RMD was previously stopped at -4.82%; basing but marginally above SMA200, lower conviction. IT is the cleanest setup.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $185.73 or better; accept fill up to $188 on strength. Prefer entry on a minor intraday pullback to the flat SMA50 zone rather than chasing.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Gartner is a capital-light research and advisory business with durable competitive moat (switching costs, subscription model). Forward P/E of 11.35 and PEG of 0.75 represent a significant discount to quality peers. ROE of 113.6% reflects exceptional capital efficiency; FCF of $1.1B on an $11.7B market cap (~9.4% FCF yield) is attractive. EPS revisions of +6.9% over 60 days suggest analyst sentiment is improving. The negative revenue growth (-0.6%) is a watch item but is offset by margin expansion and share buybacks. TECHNICAL: Price at 44% of 52-week range — in the lower-half basing zone preferred by this strategy. Confirmed uptrend (above SMA50 +4.3%, SMA200 +6.7%) with SMA50 slope +13% showing momentum. Basing pattern suggests accumulation rather than distribution. ATR of 4.3% is healthy, allowing a 1.75x ATR stop at 7.5% below entry — within the 4-15% stop band. Earnings on Nov 3 (35 days) provide a catalyst window; entry now allows position to develop before the event.
trades.exit_plan: Exit on stop at $171.75 (hard rule). Exit if price closes below SMA50 on above-average volume before target. Reduce 50% into earnings (Nov 3) if position is profitable to avoid binary event risk on full size. Full exit if thesis breaks: revenue growth deteriorates materially further negative, or if management reduces forward guidance significantly at earnings. Time stop: reassess after 90 days if price has not moved toward target.
